liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (3 reviews): The performance rolls along in a dream-like state, allowing Phil's bass to soothe the mind; The studio attempt features a divine 12-string guitar and conga drums, forming a short groove [4][10][15]

## Setlist highlights

- **Born Cross-Eyed**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 14 archived performances [16]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Dark Star [16]

## The recordings

- **gd67-11-14.sbd.unknown.17417.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 3 songs; 6 min; rated 4.58/5 by 12 [1]. Said about its sound: The studio recording quality is described as really quite good by the listener [4]
- **gd1967-11-14.116173.sbd.motb-0174.flac16**: soundboard; 2 songs; 6 min; rated 3.67/5 by 3 [2]
- **gd1967-11-14.116370.sbd.motb-0174.flac24**: soundboard; 2 songs; 6 min; rated 2.33/5 by 3 [3]

## Around the show

- Pigpen remarks near the end that the song drags right there, noting no banjo outro [3]
- This 1967 version is considered unique among all Dark Stars, being very cool and mellow [5]
- Described as a lively, no-frills studio attempt, lacking the hesitation found in later efforts [13]
- These versions differ from those on LSTIB, which feature the Anthem version with added feedback [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd67-11-14.sbd.unknown.17417.sbefail.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Likely the first recording of Dark Star, probably part of the Anthem of the Sun sessions; A remix adds keyboards, multiple vocal tracks, acid-inspired vocals, and a five-second banjo outro; The file lineage is MSR, then C1, DAT, WAV, and finally SHN format [1][11][12]
- **gd1967-11-14.116173.sbd.motb-0174.flac16**: taped by Dan Healy; transferred by Transfer By: Matt Smith & Bob Menke Mastering By: Derek McCabe; source: Source: Healy SBD [2]
- **gd1967-11-14.116370.sbd.motb-0174.flac24**: taped by Dan Healy; transferred by Matt Smith & Bob Menke Mastering By: Derek McCabe; source: SBD > ? > FLACThe Shrine ReelsTaped by: Dan HealyTransfer By: Matt Smith & Bob MenkeMastering By: Derek McCabe [3]
